summary: The candidate correctly caches and single-flights exact repeated Qwen image requests, but it is only a partial optimization. It does not provide explicit save/load operations or prompt-independent reuse by caller-selected ID, and its cache remains process-local and ephemeral.

tests.what_was_measured: At exact candidate: trusted exact-request hit, single-flight concurrency, key scoping, and bypass conditions; 4 passed. On the recorded base the copied regression immediately failed and later hung waiting for a candidate-only entrypoint, so that baseline run was terminated and retained as raw evidence.
Same content ID with two prompts generated different keys and invoked preprocessing twice; a second processor instance could not reuse the first instance's entry.
Existing cache and OpenAI protocol compatibility: 70 passed, 30 subtests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 was visible, but no Qwen-VL weights were available and the tiny Llama fixture cannot validate this architecture.

remaining_counterexamples: The same saved image content ID cannot reuse preprocessing when the rendered prompt changes because prompt text is part of the cache key.
There is no OpenAI API operation to explicitly save a preprocessing result and later load it by a caller-selected ID.
Cache entries are owned by each processor/tokenizer-worker process and are not shared across workers or preserved across restart.
Qwen video and audio requests explicitly bypass the new cache path.
remaining_limitations: No Qwen-VL weights were available for an end-to-end serving or performance measurement.
The visible MI350X GPU and tiny Llama transport fixture cannot qualify Qwen-VL preprocessing semantics.
No native files changed, so native rebuild validation was not applicable.
